newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto urges coal use boost.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto urges coal use boost.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto on Thursday urged the country to increase its utilisation of coal for its domestic energy needs.
"We have large coal reserves (of) around 31 billion tonnes. We can still increase the use of coal," Suharto said in a speech when inaugurating a coal briquettes factory in Gresik, East Java.

"Coal is one energy source that we can use easily for domestic purposes," Suharto said, adding that Indonesia would also export as much as possible other unrenewable energy sources such as oil and gas.
"Oil and gas have a high economic value but they are unrenewable resources. Therefore, we will use it as much for the people's welfare," he said.
Suharto warned that Indonesia could become an oil importer in the early next century if new reserves are not found.
"Our oil consumption continues to increase. If we do not find new reserves early in the next century then we will not have enough (oil) for our needs," he said.
"We would be forced to import oil for our needs," he said.
Indonesian coal production is expected to increase to 120 million tonnes by 2008 from 45 million tonnes in 1995, according to government figures.
Indonesia, Asia's only member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), produces around 1.57 million barrel per day of crude oil and condensate.
